### Better to Give Than to Get? Remembering God’s Promise of Reward
Author: David Mathis
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/better-to-give-than-to-get
Passage: Acts 20:35
Points:
- Paul concludes his farewell to the Ephesian elders by charging them to remember Jesus's words on generosity.
- The core of Jesus's ethic teaches that giving brings greater joy and happiness than receiving.
- God consistently promises to outgive any generosity shown to others in need.
- Remembering heavenly reward frees believers from clutching tightly to temporary earthly wealth.
- In everyday decisions, Christians can overcome reluctance by calling to mind God's promise to reward love.

### Move in the Right Direction
Author: Greg Laurie
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/harvestdaily/greg-laurie-devotion-november-1-2023.html
Passage: Acts 20:24
Points:
- Paul regarded his life as valuable only in fulfilling the specific task given to him by Jesus.
- The genuine measure of a believer's life is its contribution rather than its duration.
- Like runners in an athletic race, believers must stay focused on completing their own assignment.
- Because our lifespan is entirely determined by God, we must direct our lives toward eternity today.

### Shepherds of Christ's Flock
Author: Eric Watkins
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/shepherds-of-christs-flock
Passage: Acts 20:28
Points:
- Despite impending suffering in Jerusalem, Paul's supreme concern remained the protection of Christ's church.
- Church elders are called and equipped by the Holy Spirit to shepherd the flock sacrificially.
- The church is precious to God because He purchased her with His own blood.
- Leaders must stay vigilant against destructive false teachings emerging from both outside and within the congregation.
- Believers ought to pray for and support the faithful elders who guard their spiritual well-being.

### Day 274: Acts 20:25–31
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-274-acts-20-2531.html
Passage: Acts 20:28
Points:
- Paul prioritizes an urgent warning that leaders must guard themselves before attempting to guard others.
- Spiritual leaders cannot successfully steer others toward a course they are neglecting in their own lives.
- Anyone entrusted by God with the care of others shares the responsibility of keeping spiritual watch.
- Guarding the flock requires knowing God's Word thoroughly so as to recognize subtle distortions of the truth.
